[F8] **Cutoff and mollification on a cylinder.** Reflection across $t=0$ by $g(t,x):=f(t,x)$ for $t\ge0$ and $g(t,x):=2f(0,x)-f(-t,x)$ for $t<0$ extends $f$ to a $C^{1,2}$ function on a negative-time collar and agrees with $f$ on the nonnegative half-space. Choose compact cylinders $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ inside a bounded open set on which $g$ is defined. The cutoff lemma gives a continuous compactly supported cutoff equal to $1$ on $K'$; convolution with a sufficiently small compactly supported mollifier gives $\chi\in C_c^\infty$ equal to $1$ on $K$ and supported in that open set. Then $g_\varepsilon:=(\chi g)*\rho_\varepsilon$ is smooth and compactly supported, and on the inner cylinder the functions $g_\varepsilon,\partial_tg_\varepsilon,\partial_xg_\varepsilon,\partial^2_{xx}g_\varepsilon$ converge uniformly to $f,\partial_tf,\partial_xf,\partial^2_{xx}f$. To justify the derivative convergence, write the convolution as $\int \rho(z)(\chi g)(y-\varepsilon z)dz$. Difference quotients and the fundamental theorem in each variable move each available derivative ($\partial_t$, $\partial_x$, $\partial_{xx}$) onto $\chi g$, dominated on the fixed compact support by the corresponding continuous derivative bound times $|\rho(z)|$. On the inner cylinder $\chi=1$ on a neighbourhood; uniform continuity of each derivative bounds its convolution error by its modulus on shifts of size at most $\varepsilon R$ times $\int|\rho|$, where $R$ bounds the mollifier support. This tends to zero. [F8] **Cutoff and mollification.** Extend $f$ across $t=0$ on a small negative-time collar by $$\widetilde f(t,x)= \begin{cases}f(t,x),&t\ge0,\\3f(-t,x)-2f(-2t,x),&t<0. \end{cases}$$ The coefficients make both the value and the time derivative agree at $t=0$ ($3-2=1$ and $-3+4=1$), while the same value identity gives agreement of all spatial derivatives through order two; hence $\widetilde f$ is $C^{1,2}$ on a neighbourhood of the localized cylinder. To obtain the needed smooth cutoff from the available continuous-cutoff interface, choose compact sets $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq K'$ inside a bounded open set $O$ in that neighbourhood, take the continuous compactly supported cutoff $\eta$ that equals $1$ on $K'$, and convolve $\eta$ with a sufficiently small compactly supported unit-mass mollifier. The result $\chi$ is smooth, equals $1$ on $K$, and has support in $O$. Thus $g:=\chi\widetilde f$ is compactly supported and $C^{1,2}$, and its mollifications are smooth with $g_\varepsilon,\partial_tg_\varepsilon,\partial_ig_\varepsilon,\partial_i\partial_jg_\varepsilon$ converging uniformly to the corresponding functions on the inner cylinder. For this derivative assertion write $g_\varepsilon(y)=\int\rho(z)g(y-\varepsilon z)dz$. Difference quotients and the fundamental theorem in each variable move each available derivative $\partial_t,\partial_i,\partial_i\partial_j$ onto $g$, dominated by its continuous derivative bound on a fixed compact set times $|\rho|$. Uniform continuity bounds the error by that derivative's modulus at shifts of size $\varepsilon R$ times $\int|\rho|$, which tends to zero. No mixed time-space derivative of $f$ is assumed.
